AI quality / Cost and escalation

AI case escalation rate

The percentage of unique eligible terminal AI cases requiring a human takeover under the agreed escalation policy. Each case is counted once even if it creates several review actions or attempts.

Explore in the metric hierarchy ↗Open calculators →
Level 4Inspect the detail

The percentage of unique eligible terminal AI cases requiring a human takeover under the agreed escalation policy. Each case is counted once even if it creates several review actions or attempts.

%

How we use it

We assess which cases need human expertise and whether escalation rules protect task quality while keeping ownership clear.

Transparent calculationUnique eligible terminal AI cases escalated to a human / all unique eligible terminal AI cases in the same cohort * 100
escalated cases42
eligible terminal cases300

42 / 300 * 100 = 14% AI case escalation rate.

Illustrative calculation. Not a client result or a universal benchmark.

Break the result down

  • Case type and escalation reason
  • Risk and acceptance requirements
  • Model and workflow version

Questions we investigate

  • Which case types require repeated human takeover?
  • Are difficult cases slipping past the policy?
  • Do escalated cases reach an accountable owner?

Actions the evidence supports

  • Calibrate client-specific escalation rules.
  • Review missed and unnecessary escalations.
  • Improve context and handoff quality for reviewers.

Reporting contract

Ownership & cadence

AI operations and service leads
Weekly with reviewed missed-escalation samples.

Required data

  • Deduplicated eligible case IDs and terminal states
  • Escalation reasons, timestamps, and owners
  • Reviewed policy outcomes and system versions

Read the measure with context

Zero eligible terminal cases makes the rate undefined. Lower is not automatically better: missed necessary escalations can create harm. Distinguish routine checks from takeover, record reasons, and validate policies against reviewed outcomes; model self-confidence is not accuracy.
